title: Graph Valid Tree
statement: You get n nodes numbered 0 to n-1 and a list of undirected edges. Decide whether these edges form a tree: every node is reachable from every other, and there are no loops.

example.caption: 5 nodes and 4 edges, all reachable from node 0, no loop. That is a tree.

output.label: true: n - 1 = 4 edges and everything is reached

idea.sentence: A graph on n nodes is a tree exactly when it has n - 1 edges and a walk from one node reaches all n nodes.

jargon.plain: A connected graph with no loops. It has exactly one path between any two nodes.
Visit a node, then all its neighbours, then their neighbours, using a queue.
Every node can be reached from every other node by following edges.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the node count, then the edges, e.g. 5, [[0,1],[0,2],[0,3],[1,4]]

compare.bruteLabel: Test every pair for a path, and look for loops

rows.name: Pairwise path and loop checks
rows.note: Check reachability for each pair and search for any loop.

rows.name: Edge count + BFS
rows.note: The count check is constant time. After it, m equals n - 1, and the walk visits each node and edge once.

rows.name: Union-find (alternative)
rows.note: Fail if an edge joins two nodes already in one group. With n - 1 edges and no loop, the graph is connected.

fast.takeaway: Two facts replace a loop search. With n - 1 edges, connected and loop-free imply each other, so one reachability walk is enough.

stages.title: Count the edges
stages.note: A tree on n nodes has exactly n - 1 edges. Any other count fails at once.

stages.title: Set up the walk
stages.note: Build neighbour lists. Put node 0 in the queue and mark it reached.

stages.title: Take a node
stages.note: Pop the front node and look at its neighbours.

stages.title: Reach new nodes
stages.note: Mark each unreached neighbour and queue it. Reached ones are skipped.

stages.title: Everyone reached?
stages.note: If the queue handled all n nodes the graph is connected, and with n - 1 edges that makes it a tree.

edges.title: Single node
edges.why: Zero edges equals n - 1, and node 0 reaches itself. One lone node is a tree.

edges.title: Too few edges
edges.why: Two edges for four nodes is not 3. The count check fails before any walk.

edges.title: Right count, but a loop
edges.why: Three edges for four nodes passes the count. Node 3 is never reached, so the walk catches it.

edges.title: Too many edges
edges.why: Three edges for three nodes forms a loop. Everything is reachable, but the count is already one too high.

gotchas.text: Connectedness alone is not enough. A triangle is connected and has a loop. The edge count check is what rules loops out.
Mark a node when you queue it, not when you pop it. Otherwise a node reachable by two routes enters the queue twice and the reached count is inflated.
Array(n).fill([]) shares one array between all nodes, so every neighbour list ends up identical. Use Array.from({ length: n }, () => []).
make([][]int, n) leaves nil inner slices, and append on a nil slice is fine. make([]bool, n) is all false, so seen needs no loop to initialise.

recap.key: Fail unless there are exactly n - 1 edges, then walk from node 0 and require every node to be reached.
recap.complexity: Time O(n + m). Space O(n + m).
moves: Return false unless edges.length is n - 1
Build neighbour lists in both directions
BFS from node 0, marking nodes as they are queued
Return whether the queue handled all n nodes
